title: Invalid-instrument inference: published simulation and Card application
description:
Develop a source-assisted statistical research analysis of the B1 simulation and Appendix E.1 Card application in Guo, Zheng and Buhlmann, Robustness Against Weak or Invalid Instruments: Exploring Nonlinear Treatment Models with Machine Learning, JMLR 27(198):1-67 (2026), https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v27/24-0515.html. This is a bounded published-result case, not blind rediscovery, a new identification theorem, or reproduction of the entire article. Use the supplied pinned paper, code and data rather than remembered numerical results.

In persistent Markdown/LaTeX, define the treatment-effect estimand, structural model and candidate violation spaces. Develop a reviewable equation-level explanation of curvature identification and the estimator's bias correction. Distinguish population identification, estimator construction, fixed-space inference and data-selected-space inference. Keep assumptions attached to conclusions; state which asymptotic results are being invoked from the paper, which steps you have independently derived, and what remains unresolved. Challenge the argument and implementation with diagnostic computation and source-based checks. Numerical agreement is not a proof or validation of observational causal assumptions.

For B1, reconstruct the published heteroskedastic design and compare oracle TSCI, comparison-selected TSCI, robust-selected TSCI, TSLS, oracle RF-Init without bias correction, oracle RF-Plug and oracle RF-Full over the paper's stated settings. Preserve the published methods' distinct information access. Only the oracle comparators may receive the supplied correct violation-basis columns. Report bias, interval coverage, interval length, numerical failures and the uncertainty of the simulation summaries. Distinguish the published replication counts from any independently justified extension; specify aims, DGPs, estimands, methods, metrics, seeds, precision and stopping before confirmation. Do not require all methods to have nominal coverage. Running one configured batch is not reproducing the complete producer/aggregation grid.

For Card, reproduce the four alternative violation-space constructions in Appendix E.1 with their declared covariates and split/aggregation procedure. Explain the wage and schooling estimand, the instrument, the comparison and the sensitivity to violation spaces. This is not the main Figure 4 multi-split analysis unless you separately supply and execute that analysis. Preserve the application data and source identities; explain what the observed estimates cannot establish about instrument validity.

Implement the public run_estimator interface below in model-owned Python or R, disclosing all package and author-code reuse. Keep author sources unchanged. Label unchanged execution, adaptation and independent reimplementation separately, including any altered random-number or split conventions. If a dependency, data file, scientific definition or reference is unavailable, report the exact gap and its consequences. Do not silently substitute a homoskedastic comparator, another package version, a cached result or an invented author implementation. Available work may proceed, but an unexecuted method or missing required comparison remains incomplete. Obtain review of the current theory and executable source, use feedback to revise those same owned files, and submit the selected theory, source, simulation results and application report with their provenance and remaining gaps. Formalization is not requested and must not block this non-formal case.

request_fields.name: outcome
request_fields.units: Supplied outcome units; log wage in the Card application
request_fields.indexing: Observation order shared by all supplied data

request_fields.name: treatment
request_fields.units: Supplied treatment units; years of schooling in Card
request_fields.edge_cases: This is observed treatment, not its fitted first-stage mean

request_fields.name: instrument
request_fields.edge_cases: Continuous in B1 and binary in Card; do not force one design's support onto the other

request_fields.name: covariates
request_fields.indexing: Same observation order; column order fixed by the declared design
request_fields.edge_cases: Basis construction and intercept conventions must be disclosed in the selected source rather than inferred from a hidden true model

request_fields.name: method
request_fields.meaning: Requested published method: tsci_oracle, tsci_comparison, tsci_robust, tsls, oracle_rf_init, oracle_rf_plugin or oracle_rf_full
request_fields.indexing: One fit on the supplied sample
request_fields.edge_cases: Do not substitute another method when the requested implementation fails or is unavailable

request_fields.name: configuration
request_fields.meaning: Explicit method and candidate-basis settings declared by the model's selected source and frozen before confirmation
request_fields.units: Units defined in the selected source documentation
request_fields.indexing: Applies to the whole requested fit
request_fields.edge_cases: Defaults, basis conventions and changes from the pinned source must be documented; this field supplies no reference answer

request_fields.name: seed
request_fields.meaning: Random-number initialization for this estimator invocation
request_fields.shape: Scalar accepted by the declared execution runtime
request_fields.indexing: Controls fit randomization, not the dataset's true treatment effect
request_fields.edge_cases: Document runtime, RNG, worker streams and split conventions; adding seed control is an adaptation if the author source did not specify it

request_fields.name: oracle_basis
request_fields.meaning: Correct violation-basis columns available to oracle TSCI and the three oracle RF comparators
request_fields.shape: Finite n-by-r matrix for oracle fits; null for tsci_comparison, tsci_robust and tsls
request_fields.edge_cases: Never provide the true violation setting or oracle columns to the data-selected TSCI procedure; evaluated oracle fits require their declared basis

response_fields.name: method
response_fields.indexing: Same invocation as the remaining response
response_fields.edge_cases: Preserve this identity on a failed fit

response_fields.name: status
response_fields.meaning: completed, failed or unavailable, according to actual execution
response_fields.edge_cases: A numeric return is not evidence of convergence or statistical correctness; retain relevant diagnostics
response_fields.normalization: No success inferred from file presence or process exit alone

response_fields.name: estimate
response_fields.meaning: Estimated treatment-effect coefficient for the requested method, or null if unresolved
response_fields.indexing: The declared treatment coefficient, not an intercept or first-stage coefficient
response_fields.edge_cases: Do not return a reference, true coefficient or another method's estimate on failure

response_fields.name: standard_error
response_fields.meaning: The requested method's estimated sampling standard error, or null if unavailable
response_fields.edge_cases: A resolved point estimate can coexist with an unresolved standard error; report that distinction
response_fields.normalization: Sampling standard error, not the standard deviation of a rescaled asymptotic limit

response_fields.name: interval
response_fields.meaning: The method's nominal 95 percent confidence interval, or null if unresolved
response_fields.shape: Two ordered finite endpoints when resolved
response_fields.indexing: Lower then upper endpoint for the same fit
response_fields.edge_cases: Keep the method's declared selection/inference convention and report its conditions; nominal is not guaranteed finite-sample coverage

response_fields.name: diagnostics
response_fields.meaning: Actual warnings, numerical/selection disposition, selected basis, method configuration and provenance needed to interpret the fit
response_fields.edge_cases: Preserve missing-source and numerical failures rather than drop them from performance denominators
response_fields.normalization: No conversion of diagnostics into proof or causal-validity credit

invariants.meaning: Only oracle methods receive correct violation-basis columns. No method receives the true treatment-effect coefficient or hidden reference outcomes.
Preserve pinned author files. Document any adapter or independent implementation as such, including algorithm, variance, selection, split and random-number differences.
Each returned fit concerns exactly the supplied sample and method. Do not silently change covariates, design, method or sample size to obtain a completed return.

empirical_claims.meaning: Reconstruct the specified B1 design, execute the complete declared settings/batches and aggregate bias, interval coverage and length with uncertainty and unconditional failure counts; source execution and any independent extension remain separately labelled.
Execute and interpret the four Appendix E.1 Card alternative-basis analyses with the declared data, covariates, split and aggregation provenance; do not relabel this as the main Figure 4 analysis.
